what: is_impossible_associated_item (traits.rs:281) now calls a provided method impossible where rustdoc keeps it: blaze-doc tests::provided_methods_that_cannot_apply_are_left_out (round3d-test.log, tests.rs:569) gets ["Item"] for `impl<A: Clone> Each for Finds<A> { type Item = shapes::Square; }`, where `fn borrowed(&self) where for<'a> &'a Self::Item: Copy` must stay (a shared reference is always Copy). The same clause passes for `impl Each for Squares` and `impl<'a> Each for Borrows<'a>`, so it is the impl type parameter: in TypingMode::Coherence its fresh ?A leaves `<Finds<?A> as Each>::Item` unnormalized (?A: Clone ambiguous) and the goal under the binder comes back an error, not ambiguity. It passed before v2: the pre-v2 version (git show 8586c6e64a:crates/hir-ty/src/traits.rs) normalized each trait clause through `knowable` with structurally_normalize_ty (an alias under a binder judged as written) and skipped a goal it could not know; v2 (5719e9d7fb era) dropped that block for DbInterner::new_with(db, krate). Fix at its owner: restore that per-clause handling on top of the local-crate interner, or evaluate each clause on its own and count only a definite NoSolution as impossible (ambiguity and overflow may apply, as rustc`s is_impossible_associated_item does with `!result.may_apply()`). The test is right: rustdoc lists `borrowed` there. From tests-engine (edit-only; reads the next round`s log).
